criterion_notes.c1: Examines household access to improved drinking water sources, improved sanitation facilities, and time to water source in Ghana.
criterion_notes.c2: Fails both the plain wording of Criterion 2 and the narrow 2026-10-13 rule-type mechanism reading. Under the plain wording, the study does not examine any legal, administrative, institutional, regulatory, or governance factor; its independent variables are purely household socioeconomic, demographic, and geographic attributes (wealth index, education of household head, household size, marital status, gender of household head, administrative region, and urban/rural residence), with water-sector institutions and jurisdictional coordination mentioned only as unanalysed policy recommendations in the conclusion. Under the narrow 2026-10-13 reading, no rule-type mechanism governing service access (such as eligibility rules, tenure/documentation requirements, tariff/cost-recovery rules, administrative burden, enforcement, or regulatory/utility ownership structure) is empirically analysed.
criterion_notes.c3: Quantitative cross-sectional empirical analysis of secondary survey data from the nationally representative 2008 Ghana Demographic and Health Survey (analytic N = 11,619 for water and time models; N = 11,529 for sanitation models) using complementary log-log generalized linear models and ordinary least squares regression.
criterion_notes.c4: Reports dichotomous household access to an improved drinking water source, dichotomous access to an improved sanitation facility, and continuous travel/collection time to water source in minutes.
criterion_notes.c5: Clearly identifies the population and unit of analysis (households in Ghana from the 2008 GDHS), exposures (socioeconomic, demographic, and spatial predictors), outcomes (improved water source, improved sanitation facility, and time to water source), and study design (cross-sectional survey regression analysis), though the exposures fall outside Criterion 2.

evidence_quotes.quote: Data for the study were drawn from the Ghana 2008 Demographic and Health Survey (Ghana Statistical Service 2009).
The three major dependent variables used for this study were ‘source of drinking water’, ‘sanitation facilities’ and ‘time to water source in minutes’.
Seven independent variables comprising wealth, education, number of household members, marital status, gender of household head, region, and place of residence were used.

Finally, we recognize that lack of access to sanitation is linked to limited access to clean water. The challenge has been lack of jurisdictional coordination between the separate sectors that deal with water and sanitation issues.

raw_response.exposure: Household socioeconomic, demographic, and spatial characteristics: wealth index quintiles, household head education, household size, marital status, sex of household head, administrative region, and urban/rural place of residence (plus source of drinking water and time to water source in sanitation models).
raw_response.outcome: Household use of an improved source of drinking water (dichotomous), use of an improved sanitation facility (dichotomous), and time to water source in minutes (continuous).
raw_response.population_and_sample: Households in Ghana sampled in the 2008 Ghana Demographic and Health Survey (11,778 households surveyed; analytic sample N = 11,619 for water/time models and N = 11,529 for sanitation models).
raw_response.rationale: Excluded under E03 (Wrong exposure). Although this empirical cross-sectional study of the 2008 Ghana Demographic and Health Survey measures household access to improved drinking water and sanitation facilities, its explanatory variables are strictly household socioeconomic, demographic, and spatial predictors (wealth, education, household size, marital status, sex of household head, region, and urban/rural residence). It does not empirically examine any legal, administrative, institutional, regulatory, or governance factor under either the plain wording of Criterion 2 or the narrow 2026-10-13 rule-type mechanism scope.
raw_response.study_design: Cross-sectional quantitative secondary survey analysis (complementary log-log generalized linear models and OLS regression).
